column1: # docs/alloc-live-allow.tsv -- server.so's allocation sites still live at unload, each
# allowed with its reason (plan_server_novalve.md 3.6, the P4 exit gate).
# tools/novalve-snapshot enforces it: every live site in the allocation checker's unload
# report is resolved (addr2line over the debug server.so) to its function, argument list
# dropped, and must match a row's key exactly. A live site with no row fails the capture,
# and so does a row that matches no live site (a fixed leak takes its row out with it).
# The blocks/bytes columns are the measurement the row was reviewed at, not a limit.
# Reviewed by the user 2026-09-30. At 5fbe408 (console objects freed after
# UnregisterConCommands, the one group ruled FIX): 4873 allocations, 3903 releases,
# 0 mismatches, 0 foreign frees, 970 live at 17 sites in 9 functions.
# Nothing below is freed by the engine or by us: these are registrations the engine
# holds pointers into for as long as server.so is loaded, so nothing crosses the
# boundary (the user's rule). Each reason was checked against the allocating line.
# KNOWN LIMIT: the checker records one return address, and in a debug build that is
# the std::__new_allocator frame for any std container, so the three std:: keys name
# the ALLOCATOR, not the owner. Their owner today is the entity-class descriptors'
# ss::StringPool (shell_standalone_class.cpp:297), but a leak of any other std
# container would pass under the same key. Follow-up: record the first frame outside
# std:: at allocation.
